name: TX-31
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent John Carter running with large fundraising edge
Democrat Justin Early badly outraised and low on cash
Prediction markets give Democrats only ~6% chance
model.rationale: The R+11 baseline, Carter's incumbency and roughly 11-to-1 fundraising advantage, and a Polymarket price near 95% Republican all point the same direction. With no polls or expert ratings to justify moving off the quantitative baseline, I hold near its -14.7 margin.
model.watch: A late Democratic outside-spending surge or a broad Texas suburban shift toward Democrats could tighten the race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 31st District leans firmly Republican, with a partisan baseline of about R+11, and longtime incumbent John Carter is running for reelection after easily securing his party's nomination. Carter has raised roughly $1.4 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Democratic nominee Justin Early has raised only about $124,000 with minimal cash on hand. No outside groups are opposing Carter.

There are no public general-election polls or expert ratings for this race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals, fundraising, and prediction markets, which give Democrats only about a 6 percent chance. The expected outcome is a comfortable Republican win, though the absence of polling adds some uncertainty to the exact margin.
